name: SDN HTTP Respond
description: The HTTP edge's responder (typed contracts 1.0): a typed decision plus the typed answer in, exactly one $HTR HttpResponse envelope out. Method respond takes the SDS $APR (API Request) decision and at most one body ($NHS node health, $NEV node events, $NST peers, $PNV publication verdicts, or a $DAV dataset availability with the dataset's records on its standard's *_records port); method respond_query takes the SDS $QRP (Query Page) decision and the $QRP page stream (page header + record frames, a projection, or the query surface). Status comes from the decision ($APR STATUS; a $QRP KIND Error's HTTP_STATUS, else derived from its ERROR_CODE), 304 when If-None-Match ($APR IF_NONE_MATCH / the $QRP request's ETAG) equals the answer's entity tag ($QRP page ETAG, $NST / $PNV / $DAV ETAG), else 200. FlatBuffer bodies go out verbatim (application/x-flatbuffers for one record, application/vnd.sdn.flatbuffers.stream for a stream); JSON is rendered here and only here, when the decision's ACCEPT / REPRESENTATION asks for Json: the public API's external representation, IDL field names exactly. No JSON travels between modules. Out-of-band delivery: a $QRP page header or a $DAV carrying BODY_REF_TOKEN / BODY_REF_SIZE answers the $HTR with BODY_REF_TOKEN / BODY_REF_SIZE and no inline body (the host egress substitutes the record stream it holds). $APR RESPONSE_HEADERS (a serving stage's own headers, e.g. cache freshness) are added to the answer: lower-cased, CR/LF stripped, the computed names refused, at most 16, values at most 1 KiB. Pure compute - no capabilities.

acceptedTypeSets.description: $APR: the decision foundation/http-route made, passed on by the serving node verbatim, or with STATUS / ERROR_CODE / ERROR_MESSAGE set when the request was refused or could not be served. ACCEPT selects the representation; IF_NONE_MATCH the conditional request.

inputPorts.description: The decision.

acceptedTypeSets.description: Canonical WASM-served HTTP response envelope ($HTR, module-sdk schemas/HttpResponseAbi.fbs): STATUS, HEADERS (sorted, lower-cased names), BODY. The host streams it back verbatim.

methods.description: Answers an $APR-decided request. A refusal (STATUS set) without a body answers its STATUS with the $APR itself (FlatBuffer) or {"error":ERROR_MESSAGE,"code":ERROR_CODE} (Json); with a body beside it (503 + the $DAV of an unavailable dataset) the body is the answer at that STATUS. 304 when IF_NONE_MATCH equals the answer's ETAG ($NST, $PNV, $DAV). A $DAV with BODY_REF_TOKEN answers by reference (no inline body). RESPONSE_HEADERS ride the answer. Otherwise 200: FlatBuffer/Default -> the record verbatim (application/x-flatbuffers, x-sdn-file-identifier) or, for a dataset, one size-prefixed stream of its $DAV followed by its records (application/vnd.sdn.flatbuffers.stream, x-sdn-record-count); Json -> the record rendered with its IDL field names (enums by name, byte vectors hex), a dataset as a bare array of its records ($OMM only; another standard answers 406); Csv/Text -> 406. A decision served without any body answers 502. BATCHING: every input port is single-stream BY CONTRACT (one HTTP exchange) and that is ENFORCED IN CODE: the compiled flow runtime drains a node's whole queue port-blind (maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are declarative only), so two frames on one port - e.g. a router's refusal and a serving node's decision, which flows wire into the same "decision" port and which are mutually exclusive by construction - are refused with error code "batched-input-frames" rather than answered from whichever frame the queue held first (graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames). Bodies on two different ports are refused too ("ambiguous-body").

acceptedTypeSets.description: $QRP: the request foundation/http-route decided, passed on verbatim by the serving node, or a KIND Error (from the router's "refusal" port or the serving node). REPRESENTATION selects the representation; ETAG is the client's If-None-Match.

inputPorts.description: The decision.

acceptedTypeSets.description: The $QRP page stream: a size-prefixed QRP KIND Page header (ETAG, RECORD_COUNT, FILE_IDENTIFIER; or COLUMNS + ROWS for a projection; or TABLES + MAX_* for the query surface) followed by RECORD_COUNT size-prefixed record frames of the named standard.

inputPorts.description: The answer, absent on a refusal.

acceptedTypeSets.description: Canonical WASM-served HTTP response envelope ($HTR, module-sdk schemas/HttpResponseAbi.fbs): STATUS, HEADERS (sorted, lower-cased names), BODY. The host streams it back verbatim.

methods.description: Answers a $QRP-decided request. A KIND Error (decision or page header) answers its HTTP_STATUS, or when that is 0 the status its ERROR_CODE names: no-route/not-found 404, method-not-allowed 405, not-acceptable 406, timeout/too-large 422, host-failed 502, unavailable 503 (and any STATUS Busy/Cold, with retry-after from RETRY_AFTER_MS), any other code 400 - with the $QRP itself (FlatBuffer) or {"error":MESSAGE,"code":ERROR_CODE} (Json). 304 when the request's ETAG equals the page header's ETAG. A page header carrying BODY_REF_TOKEN answers by reference: the $HTR names the host's token, no inline body. Otherwise 200: FlatBuffer/Default -> the page stream verbatim (application/vnd.sdn.flatbuffers.stream, x-sdn-record-count, etag); Json -> a bare array of the page's records ($OMM only; another standard answers 406), a projection as a bare array of {COLUMN: value} objects (bytes base64), or the query surface as {"TABLES","MAX_ELAPSED_MS","MAX_ROWS","MAX_BYTES"}. A request served without a page answers 502. BATCHING: every input port is single-stream BY CONTRACT (one HTTP exchange) and that is ENFORCED IN CODE: the compiled flow runtime drains a node's whole queue port-blind (maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are declarative only), so two frames on one port - e.g. a router's refusal and a serving node's decision, which flows wire into the same "decision" port and which are mutually exclusive by construction - are refused with error code "batched-input-frames" rather than answered from whichever frame the queue held first (graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames). Bodies on two different ports are refused too ("ambiguous-body").
